title: Decoupled tool-resolution and streaming shim for OpenAI-style tool calls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a decoupled runtime shim that translates OpenAI-style tool declarations and invocations into our legacy function signature model while preserving streaming semantics, provenance, and structured output guarantees. The shim should operate as a lightweight resolution layer that: (1) resolves tool name aliases and tenant-specific mappings, (2) validates and coerces arguments into legacy function parameter shapes, (3) supports partial/streaming tool outputs (incremental events) and reconciles them with the LLM streaming API, and (4) emits observability events for mapping decisions and fallbacks. This reduces user friction for integrations that rely on OpenAI 'tool' conventions and prevents forcing a cross-cutting migration in customer codebases.
acceptance_criteria: Shim resolves OpenAI-style tool names to legacy function identifiers using a canonical registry and per-tenant alias table
Argument coercion layer supports JSON schema-based coercion and emits validation errors as structured tokens instead of raw failure traces
Streaming tool responses (partial JSON/text events) are forwarded to clients preserving order and incremental flush semantics
Fallback path when no mapping exists: return structured 'suggested-mapping' metadata and optionally call a safe noop function under a configurable policy
End-to-end integration tests for at least three real functions (search, calendar.create, image.generate) passed in CI
Metrics emitted: mapping_resolution_latency, mapping_confidence, streaming_event_rate, mapping_fallback_count
tasks: Design canonical registry data model and tenant alias table (Confluence: /display/INF/Tool+Interop+Registry)
Implement resolver service (stateless) with HTTP/grpc interface and caching layer
Implement argument coercion module using existing JSON schema lib and add type coercion rules for dates, ids, and enums
Extend runtime streaming proxy to handle intermediate tool events and ensure backpressure is respected
Add migration backfill job to generate alias suggestions from historical invocation logs
Create integration test harness and QA checklist for canary rollout
Instrument metrics and tracing spans, add dashboards to Console

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Name collisions leading to incorrect resolution for multi-tenant prefixes. Mitigation: tenant-scoped alias table with deterministic precedence and a confidence score returned to callers.
Risk: Streaming backpressure mismatch between LLM client and legacy function sinks. Mitigation: implement configurable buffering with soft limits and drop policies with observability alerts.
Risk: Increased tail latency due to resolver lookups. Mitigation: local LRU cache + warmed entries from backfill job and metric-driven cache size tuning.
qa_plan: Unit tests for resolver and coercion rules
Integration tests exercising streaming partial events and finalization semantics
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with monitoring for mapping_fallback_count and error-rate regressions
Manual exploratory tests where assistant triggers ambiguous tool names and operator verifies suggested mapping metadata
notes: Trade-offs discussed: embedding-based fuzzy resolver vs exact alias registry. Decided to use exact + heuristic suggestions (embedding only used as non-blocking hint) to avoid silent mis-invocations.
We intentionally avoid altering the legacy function surface; the shim performs translations at call time so existing internal customers do not need to change code immediately.
Plan to publish migration guide and a deprecation timeline if customers adopt OpenAI-style tool naming as first-class API surface.
